albums.blurb: Bobby Hutcherson was Blue Note's defining vibraphonist of the 1960s, and Happenings — recorded in February 1966 with Herbie Hancock on piano, Bob Cranshaw on bass and Joe Chambers on drums — was the first of his records to put him out front of a conventional rhythm section rather than the larger, more avant-garde lineups of his earlier dates. Six of the seven tunes are Hutcherson originals, alongside the definitive small-group reading of Hancock's "Maiden Voyage"; the closer "The Omen" dissolves into free percussion, with Hancock credited on a "box full of rocks". The whole session is instrumental.
albums.reception: DownBeat gave the album a five-star review, and Blue Note returned it to print in its audiophile Classic Vinyl reissue series in 2024.

albums.blurb: Orion Sun is the project of Tiffany Majette, a New Jersey-raised, Philadelphia-based singer and producer who recorded her early music at home before signing to the independent label Mom + Pop. Hold Space for Me, released in March 2020, is her studio debut, following the self-released 2017 collection A Collection of Fleeting Moments and Daydreams; she produced most of it herself, folding jazz samples and homemade beats under close-mic'd vocals.
albums.reception: KEXP named the single "Ne Me Quitte Pas (Don't Leave Me)" a Song of the Day in June 2020, and the track became the album's streaming breakout, with Atwood Magazine noting it had gone viral on Spotify.

albums.blurb: Donny Hathaway was a classically trained pianist out of Howard University who worked around Chicago as a session player, arranger and producer — including for Curtis Mayfield's Curtom label — before stepping out as a performer. Everything Is Everything, his 1970 debut on Atlantic's Atco imprint, co-produced with drummer Ric Powell, is where his gospel-rooted voice and orchestral soul arranging first came together: he co-wrote "The Ghetto" with Leroy Hutson and reworked Nina Simone's "To Be Young, Gifted and Black". The celebrated Roberta Flack duets and his live album were still ahead of him.
albums.reception: The album peaked at No. 73 on the Billboard 200 and No. 33 on Billboard's R&B albums chart, carried by the single "The Ghetto".
